{"type":"tool_use","timestamp":1792963621437,"sessionID":"ses_e8b0b551affeuGl57c4wDMjNX2","part":{"type":"tool","tool":"write","callID":"toolu_01HxXkdkB4P8GSQ75UC4nvsN","state":{"status":"completed","input":{"filePath":"/home/llmtest/evals/20261025-170040/matmul_claude-haiku-5.5-oc-medium_mpi_r1/matmul/matmul.cpp","content":"#include <mpi.h>\n\n#include <algorithm>\n#include <chrono>\n#include <climits>\n#include <cmath>\n#include <cstdio>\n#include <cstdlib>\n#include <cstring>\n#include <vector>\n\n#include \"../common/results_output.hpp\"\n\n// Generate pseudo-random values for matrix initialization\nconstexpr double getPseudoRndValue(const size_t N, const size_t i, const size_t j) noexcept {\n    return (((i + 1) * (i + j + 1) * 1299709) % (N * N)) / static_cast<double>(N * N);\n}\n\nvoid initMatrix(std::vector<double>& mat, const size_t N) {\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < N; ++i) {\n        for (size_t j = 0; j < N; ++j) {\n            mat[i * N + j] = getPseudoRndValue(N, i, j);\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// Contiguous block of rows [begin, begin + count) owned by one rank\nstruct RowRange {\n    size_t begin;\n    size_t count;\n};\n\nRowRange rowRangeFor(const size_t N, const int rank, const int size) {\n    const size_t r = static_cast<size_t>(rank);\n    const size_t p = static_cast<size_t>(size);\n    const size_t base = N / p;\n    const size_t rem = N % p;\n    return {r * base + std::min(r, rem), base + (r < rem ? 1 : 0)};\n}\n\n// Computes C = A * B for `rows` local rows.\n//   A: rows x N slice of the full matrix (row-major)\n//   B: full N x N matrix (row-major)\n//   C: rows x N output, must be zero-initialized\n// Each C element accumulates its k-terms in ascending k order, exactly as the\n// naive triple loop does, so results are bitwise identical to the serial code.\n// The k-dimension is blocked so a panel of B stays cache-resident while four\n// rows of C are updated together, reusing each loaded B element four times.\nvoid matrixMultiplyRows(const double* A, const double* B, double* C,\n                        const size_t rows, const size_t N) {\n    constexpr size_t KB = 64;\n\n    for (size_t kk = 0; kk < N; kk += KB) {\n        const size_t kEnd = std::min(kk + KB, N);\n\n        size_t i = 0;\n        for (; i + 4 <= rows; i += 4) {\n            const double* a0 = A + (i + 0) * N;\n            const double* a1 = A + (i + 1) * N;\n            const double* a2 = A + (i + 2) * N;\n            const double* a3 = A + (i + 3) * N;\n            double* c0 = C + (i + 0) * N;\n            double* c1 = C + (i + 1) * N;\n            double* c2 = C + (i + 2) * N;\n            double* c3 = C + (i + 3) * N;\n\n            for (size_t k = kk; k < kEnd; ++k) {\n                const double x0 = a0[k];\n                const double x1 = a1[k];\n                const double x2 = a2[k];\n                const double x3 = a3[k];\n                const double* b = B + k * N;\n                for (size_t j = 0; j < N; ++j) {\n                    const double bj = b[j];\n                    c0[j] += x0 * bj;\n                    c1[j] += x1 * bj;\n                    c2[j] += x2 * bj;\n                    c3[j] += x3 * bj;\n                }\n            }\n        }\n\n        for (; i < rows; ++i) {\n            const double* a = A + i * N;\n            double* c = C + i * N;\n            for (size_t k = kk; k < kEnd; ++k) {\n                const double x = a[k];\n                const double* b = B + k * N;\n                for (size_t j = 0; j < N; ++j) {\n                    c[j] += x * b[j];\n                }\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// Simple validation: compute a single element and compare\nbool validateResult(const std::vector<double>& A, const std::vector<double>& B,\n                   const std::vector<double>& C, const size_t N) {\n    // Check a few random positions\n    constexpr size_t checkPoints[] = {0, 1, 2, 3, 4};\n    \n    for (size_t pi = 0; pi < 5; ++pi) {\n        for (size_t pj = 0; pj < 5; ++pj) {\n            const size_t i = checkPoints[pi] % N;\n            const size_t j = checkPoints[pj] % N;\n            \n            double expected = 0.0;\n            for (size_t k = 0; k < N; ++k) {\n                expected += A[i * N + k] * B[k * N + j];\n            }\n            \n            const double actual = C[i * N + j];\n            const double relError = std::abs((actual - expected) / (expected + 1e-10));\n            \n            if (relError > 1e-6) {\n                printf(\"Validation failed at (%zu, %zu): expected %.10f, got %.10f (error: %.10e)\\n\",\n                       i, j, expected, actual, relError);\n                return false;\n            }\n        }\n    }\n    \n    return true;\n}\n\nvoid printUsage(const char* progName) {\n    printf(\"Usage: %s [options]\\n\", progName);\n    printf(\"Options:\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -n <num>     Matrix size N (computes NxN * NxN) (default: 512)\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -v           Enable validation\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -r           Print results for external validation\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -h           Show this help message\\n\");\n}\n\n// Runs the benchmark on all ranks; only rank 0 prints. Returns the exit status.\nint runBenchmark(const int rank, const int size, const size_t N,\n                 const bool validate, const bool printResults) {\n    const bool root = (rank == 0);\n    MPI_Comm comm = MPI_COMM_WORLD;\n\n    if (root) {\n        printf(\"Matrix Multiplication Benchmark\\n\");\n        printf(\"Matrix size: %zu x %zu\\n\", N, N);\n        printf(\"Validation: %s\\n\", validate ? \"enabled\" : \"disabled\");\n        printf(\"MPI ranks: %d\\n\", size);\n        printf(\"Initializing matrices...\\n\");\n    }\n\n    // A and B are deterministic, so every rank generates them locally rather\n    // than receiving them over the network.\n    std::vector<double> A(N * N);\n    std::vector<double> B(N * N);\n    initMatrix(A, N);\n    initMatrix(B, N);\n\n    const RowRange myRows = rowRangeFor(N, rank, size);\n    std::vector<double> Clocal(myRows.count * N, 0.0);\n\n    if (root) {\n        printf(\"Computing matrix multiplication...\\n\");\n    }\n\n    // Time the distributed multiplication: synchronize, compute, and report\n    // the slowest rank's elapsed time.\n    MPI_Barrier(comm);\n    auto start = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();\n\n    matrixMultiplyRows(A.data() + myRows.begin * N, B.data(), Clocal.data(), myRows.count, N);\n\n    auto end = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();\n    const double localMs = std::chrono::duration<double, std::milli>(end - start).count();\n    double maxMs = 0.0;\n    MPI_Reduce(&localMs, &maxMs, 1, MPI_DOUBLE, MPI_MAX, 0, comm);\n\n    if (root) {\n        auto duration = std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::milliseconds>(\n            std::chrono::duration<double, std::milli>(maxMs));\n\n        printf(\"Computation time: %ld ms\\n\", duration.count());\n\n        // Calculate GFLOPS\n        double gflops = (2.0 * N * N * N) / (duration.count() / 1000.0) / 1e9;\n        printf(\"Performance: %.3f GFLOPS\\n\", gflops);\n    }\n\n    // Gather the full C matrix on rank 0 only when it is needed for output or\n    // validation. Row blocks are gathered as contiguous rows of N doubles, so\n    // the MPI counts stay within int range for any N that fits in int.\n    const bool needFullC = printResults || validate;\n    std::vector<double> C;\n    if (needFullC) {\n        if (root) {\n            C.resize(N * N);\n        }\n\n        MPI_Datatype rowType;\n        MPI_Type_contiguous(static_cast<int>(N), MPI_DOUBLE, &rowType);\n        MPI_Type_commit(&rowType);\n\n        std::vector<int> counts(size), displs(size);\n        for (int r = 0; r < size; ++r) {\n            const RowRange rr = rowRangeFor(N, r, size);\n            counts[r] = static_cast<int>(rr.count);\n            displs[r] = static_cast<int>(rr.begin);\n        }\n\n        MPI_Gatherv(Clocal.data(), static_cast<int>(myRows.count), rowType,\n                    C.data(), counts.data(), displs.data(), rowType, 0, comm);\n\n        MPI_Type_free(&rowType);\n    }\n\n    if (!root) {\n        return 0;\n    }\n\n    // Print results for external validation\n    if (printResults) {\n        print_results(C, \"MatrixC\");\n    }\n\n    // Validation\n    if (validate) {\n        printf(\"Validating result...\\n\");\n        bool valid = validateResult(A, B, C, N);\n        \n        if (valid) {\n            printf(\"Validation: PASSED\\n\");\n            return 0;\n        } else {\n            printf(\"Validation: FAILED\\n\");\n            return 1;\n        }\n    }\n\n    return 0;\n}\n\nint main(int argc, char** argv) {\n    MPI_Init(&argc, &argv);\n\n    int rank = 0;\n    int size = 1;\n    MPI_Comm_rank(MPI_COMM_WORLD, &rank);\n    MPI_Comm_size(MPI_COMM_WORLD, &size);\n\n    size_t N = 512;\n    bool validate = false;\n    bool printResults = false;\n    int status = 0;\n    bool run = true;\n    \n    // Parse command line arguments (identically on every rank)\n    for (int i = 1; i < argc; ++i) {\n        if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-n\") == 0 && i + 1 < argc) {\n            N = atoi(argv[++i]);\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-v\") == 0) {\n            validate = true;\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-r\") == 0) {\n            printResults = true;\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-h\") == 0) {\n            if (rank == 0) {\n                printUsage(argv[0]);\n            }\n            run = false;\n            break;\n        } else {\n            if (rank == 0) {\n                printf(\"Unknown option: %s\\n\", argv[i]);\n                printUsage(argv[0]);\n            }\n            status = 1;\n            run = false;\n            break;\n        }\n    }\n\n    if (run) {\n        status = runBenchmark(rank, size, N, validate, printResults);\n    }\n\n    MPI_Finalize();\n    return status;\n}\n"},"output":"Wrote file successfully.","metadata":{"diagnostics":{},"filepath":"/home/llmtest/evals/20261025-170040/matmul_claude-haiku-5.5-oc-medium_mpi_r1/matmul/matmul.cpp","exists":true,"truncated":false},"title":"home/llmtest/evals/20261025-170040/matmul_claude-haiku-5.5-oc-medium_mpi_r1/matmul/matmul.cpp","time":{"start":1792963621315,"end":1792963621380}},"metadata":{"anthropic":{"caller":{"type":"direct"}}},"id":"prt_174f585dd001tmPeDTkRXUdITU","sessionID":"ses_e8b0b551affeuGl57c4wDMjNX2","messageID":"msg_174f57e5c001gjLo9efw0yt1Jj"}}

{"type":"reasoning","timestamp":1792963834457,"sessionID":"ses_e8b0b551affeuGl57c4wDMjNX2","part":{"id":"prt_174f8c8380017UFqLPbwskzsfv","messageID":"msg_174f8c491001cSMNGB8n2UEot5","sessionID":"ses_e8b0b551affeuGl57c4wDMjNX2","type":"reasoning","text":"I'm noticing GCC vectorized the k-reduction as a 2-wide SLP pair, using vmulpd with sequential vaddsd for the main loop (non-FMA, in-order) while the tail uses FMA — so the arithmetic order stays the same: products computed in pairs but summed sequentially as (sum + even) + odd.\n\nBut then the final term is special-cased as FMA when N is odd, meaning the original's exact rounding depends on parity and compiler quirks I can't cleanly replicate without hacky special-casing of the last index. Matching the non-FMA, mul-then-add semantics (equivalent to -ffp-contract=off) covers the dominant path, but true bitwise equivalence for odd N isn't achievable without mimicking a compiler-specific artifact I'd rather not hardcode.\n\nGiven the task only requires equivalent mathematical semantics and the error tolerance is 1e-6, I'll settle on deterministic non-FMA arithmetic that's rank-count independent, since that's the practical property that matters rather than chasing bit-for-bit matches with a specific compiler's vectorization choice.\n\nThe original binary's vectorizer-driven contraction isn't something I can replicate cleanly. The more reliable fix is adding -ffp-contract=off at the build level, since that makes both clang and gcc deterministic and matches the original's off-contraction output (9e54 for N=37) exactly.\n\nI'll remove the explicit fma call, keep plain multiply-add in the kernel, and rely on the compiler flag for determinism — accepting a small performance cost since this is likely memory-bound anyway. Given the correctness requirement, deterministic documented arithmetic wins over matching the default-contracted behavior, so I'll proceed with this approach and verify bitwise equality across various N and P values.\n\n","time":{"start":1792963823672,"end":1792963834394},"metadata":{"anthropic":{"signature":""}}}}
{"type":"text","timestamp":1792963834458,"sessionID":"ses_e8b0b551affeuGl57c4wDMjNX2","part":{"id":"prt_174f8f21f001s074F3J18U5DD0","messageID":"msg_174f8c491001cSMNGB8n2UEot5","sessionID":"ses_e8b0b551affeuGl57c4wDMjNX2","type":"text","text":"The cause is now clear. GCC vectorized the original's k-reduction in pairs: it does separate multiply and add for most terms, and only uses an FMA for the odd leftover term. So the original's last bits depend on the compiler's vectorization choices, not on the source expression. No hand-written kernel can reproduce that exactly.\n\nThe reliable fix is to make the arithmetic explicit: disable floating-point contraction for the target with `-ffp-contract=off`, so every term is a rounded multiply followed by a rounded add, in ascending k order. The original built with the same flag gives the same results, and the MPI version is then bitwise-identical to it at any rank count. I'll remove the explicit `std::fma` and add the flag.","time":{"start":1792963834399,"end":1792963834417}}}
